decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-11-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka continues to face a profound and persistent problem of road accidents and loss of life and the average annual fatality rate in the country over the past three years, has been reported as 11.2 per 10,000 due to road accidents. This is well above the safe threshold recommended by the Second Global Decade of Action for Road Safety (2021-2030) and endorsed by the United Nations. According to data and reports of the Department of Police, 118,697 road accidents were reported in the country during the period 2020 - 2024, resulting in 12,322 deaths. Further, it has also been reported that about 400 accidents occur annually due to unprotected railway crossings. Therefore, it has been identified that it is essential to improve the quality of road infrastructure, ensure the use of safe vehicles and regulate those vehicles in order to create a safe and equitable road environment for all road users by reducing the continuous increase of number of deaths and injuries due to road accidents. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Acting Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to implement the 'Road Safety Action Plan 2025 - 2026', which has been prepared with the said objectives, was approved by the Cabinet.
